label: the chapter pages — the bottom toolbar collapses on the way down, behind ?scroll=edge for Wil's phone: a plain document with a fixed, hit-testable strip on the top edge asking Safari to paint the top bar solid; the approved default (the still document) untouched
notes: Wil, 2026-09-22, after approving round 38 live ('Works great!'): 'The only thing I want is the bottom bar to disappear when the user scrolls down. no other changes.' Told first that Safari collapses its bars only when the document scrolls and collapses both together, so the still document's static top fill and a collapsing toolbar cannot coexist by page paint; he reaffirmed. Device-first (CLAUDE.md rule 4): the mode ships behind ?scroll=edge with the default untouched — off the flag every route is byte-identical (qa:snap must hold at 0 drift; qa:still's default checks unchanged) — and becomes the default only after his read. The mode: a plain document (bars collapse and return natively; the toolbar glass over the chapter's in-flow text) plus .edge-trigger, a fixed, invisible, hit-testable 8px strip on the top edge, so Safari's edge probe finds a fixed element there and paints the top bar as an opaque fill in <body>'s colour (round 24's measured rule; round 23 pass 16's transparent-fixed-main observation). &band=<px> is the visible-band variant (the strip takes <body>'s colour by inheritance) if the invisible strip leaves the top bar glass. Round 23's pass 17 shipped this same idea as the DEFAULT on assumption and was reverted by round 38 unread; this round puts it where it belongs, behind a flag, for the phone to decide. qa:still gains the flag's checks. Numbered 40: round 39 (the map to the museum's Mapbox account) is committed on a local branch, held by GitHub's secret-scanning rule until the token is allowed, and is not in this tree.
